subject: Re: Request — Incident notification expectations & DPA evidence
messages:
From: Emma Sullivan <emma.sullivan@finexcorp.com>
To: support@redwood.com
Cc: legal@finexcorp.com
Date: 2026-04-07T08:12:00Z
Subject: Potential data exposure — clarification requested under DPA

Hi —

We noticed unusual API access patterns in our logs this morning that appear to return a subset of customer identifiers for one of our apps integrated with Redwood. At this stage we are still investigating and don't know whether any PII was actually exposed to an unauthorized third party.

Per section 6 of our DPA, we need to understand Redwood's notification commitments, the scope of information you will provide, and the expected timelines for notification to our security and legal teams. Specifically:
- When will Redwood notify us if your investigation confirms unauthorized access affecting our data?
- What evidence will you provide (logs, forensics, redacted samples)?
- Will you disclose subprocessors involved and any cross-border transfers?
- How will coordination for remediation and customer-facing disclosures work?

Please treat this as urgent — our incident response team is standing by.

Regards,
Emma Sullivan
Senior Counsel, FinexCorp
emma.sullivan@finexcorp.com

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Emma Sullivan <emma.sullivan@finexcorp.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-07T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Potential data exposure — clarification requested under DPA

Emma — thanks for flagging and for the clear list of asks. A quick acknowledgement: we received your message and have opened an incident (JIRA-RED-942).

Next steps from our side:
1) Monica (sec) will do an initial containment and confirm whether the traffic indicates unauth access or a misconfiguration.
2) Neha (legal) will review the DPA clauses and draft the notification language and a list of required evidentiary artifacts.
3) I'll coordinate the communications cadence with your team and share a proposed playbook within 24 hours.

We will aim to provide an initial technical summary within 12 hours and a firm notification determination within 48 hours unless we surface complexities requiring more time.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-07T10:30:00Z
Subject: Draft incident notification playbook (DPA-aligned) — please review

Team — I put together a short draft playbook to align our internal response and our reply to FinexCorp. Key points (summary):

- Trigger for customer notification: "Confirmed unauthorized access affecting Customer Personal Data." We should avoid promising notifications on "suspected" events unless we can validate.
- Timeline: initial acknowledgement within 4 hours (we already did this). Preliminary technical summary within 12–24 hours. Formal customer notification (if confirmed) within 48 hours of confirmation, with an aim to provide forensic artifacts within 5 business days.
  - Rationale: GDPR supervisory authority notification is 72 hours from becoming aware; customers typically require a faster practical cadence — 48 hours gives us a reasonable operational window while keeping legal alignment.
- Scope of artifacts: redacted access logs, query samples, list of API keys/roles implicated, affected data classes (IDs vs PII), and a narrative of containment steps. Avoid providing unredacted full data exports unless legally compelled.
- Subprocessors: provide the current DPA exhibit and call out any subprocessors involved in the request handling (e.g., analytics, logging vendors). If a subprocessor was implicated we will commit to an immediate notification to the customer and initiate contractual escalation with the subprocessor.
- Cross-border transfers: if data moved across regions in the course of the event, we will disclose transfer paths and safeguards (SCCs, encryption in transit).
- Cooperation & evidence: commit to a single point of contact (SEC_INCIDENT@redwood.com), regular syncs, and a 24/7 warroom for critical PII impact.

Open questions for the group:
1) Is 48 hours for customer notification acceptable to Sales/CS?
2) Can Security provide a template redacted log export (and an example attached) we can send?
3) Legal: confirm limiting language around not providing full unredacted datasets.

Attaching a working playbook PDF and a scrubbed sample log (for review).

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-07T12:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Draft incident notification playbook (DPA-aligned) — customer expectations

Agree with Neha's approach. From CS perspective: FinexCorp will expect clear answers on three fronts — scope (which of their tenant(s)/apps), duration (how long the window of exposure was), and customer impact (what end-user data types are implicated).

Notes:
- We should confirm whether FinexCorp wants us to trigger their customer notifications (i.e., whether they prefer us to draft template language for them) or whether they will handle external comms themselves. I'll ask Emma in my next reply.
- Also confirm whether they want the full subprocessors exhibit or only those involved in the handling path for the affected app — I recommend limiting to the latter to prevent confusion.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: monica_patel@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-08T02:41:00Z
Subject: Re: Draft incident notification playbook (DPA-aligned) — technical scope & artifacts

Quick technical update (initial triage complete):
- We saw anomalous read requests from a non-standard client token between 2026-04-06T22:14:00Z and 2026-04-06T22:29:00Z aimed at a single tenant namespace associated with FinexCorp.
- The requests returned resource identifiers and some metadata fields; there is no evidence so far that full PII payloads were exfiltrated.
- Containment action: rotated the compromised API token, blocked the source IPs, and revoked the session.

Artifacts I can provide for FinexCorp:
- Redacted access_logs_subset.csv (attached stub) — shows request timestamps, obfuscated API keys, endpoints called.
- Query sample (redacted) — example of returned payload schema with identifiers masked.
- SOC2-report-2025.pdf (for trust context) and current subprocessors exhibit (DPA-exhibit-subprocessors.pdf).

I recommend we keep the customer notification language conservative: say "temporary unauthorized access to a subset of API responses" and list our containment steps. If they request raw payloads we should require a legal basis and a signed NDA or limited-purpose evidence-sharing agreement.

I'll join the customer warroom and can be on the FinexCorp call later today.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Director, Security Operations, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Potential data exposure — proposed notification timeline & artifacts

Emma — thanks for your patience as we triaged. Below is a consolidated, actionable proposal from Redwood: 

1) Determination & notification timeline
- Initial ack: completed 2026-04-07T09:05Z.
- Preliminary technical summary: provided within 12 hours of this message (we attached a redacted log sample).
- Customer notification (if we confirm unauthorized access to FinexCorp data): we will notify FinexCorp within 48 hours of confirmation. We will notify supervisory authorities as required by law (we note GDPR's 72-hour standard applies to supervisory notifications).

2) Scope & artifacts we will provide
- Redacted access logs showing timestamps, obfuscated keys, and endpoints called (attached: access_logs_subset.csv).
- A redacted query/payload sample illustrating returned schema (identifiers masked).
- A list of implicated subprocessors that were involved in the request path (attached as DPA exhibit).
- SOC2 report and a technical timeline of containment and remediation steps.

3) Cooperation & next steps
- Point of contact: SEC_INCIDENT@redwood.com (warroom access for FinexCorp).
- We will schedule a technical call within 6 hours to walk through artifacts and answer questions.
- If FinexCorp requests unredacted payloads, we will require a limited-purpose evidence-sharing agreement; we will not provide unredacted exports by default.

Please confirm if FinexCorp accepts this timeline and list of artifacts. Once you confirm, we'll share a cleaned playbook PDF and make the warroom live.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
